parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Welcome to this lecture in the Health Sciences intended to inspire you and get you thinking about your research project. Today, I want to show you how even ordinary human behavior like sneezing, which normally happens when you get a cold, may be worth studying.

Have you ever been walking outside when a bright shaft of sunlight hits you between the eyes? The reaction of some people is immediate, an unpleasant prickling in the nose, an increase in their breathing rate, and an uncontrollable watering of the eyes. Then, almost as quickly, they sneeze and gain relief. This may happen every time they go into the sun.

This so-called photic or light sneeze is a reflex, which means it can't be controlled, and it's very common, anything between one in ten and one in three people might be affected.

In fact, a sneeze is triggered by an irritation of some sort in the linings of the nostrils. The result is a cascade of reactions, beginning with the stimulation of the nerve endings all over the face, and generating an explosive expulsion of air at up to 95 miles an hour; like an extremely localized personal hurricane. The body's coordination of such reactions is complicated and belongs to the subconscious control hardware that regulates other things, for example tears in the eyes.

People have been interested in the phenomenon of photic sneezing for thousands of years. The Greek philosopher Aristotle asked, why does the sun prompt us to sneeze, whereas the heat of a fire does not?

A partial answer came two thousand years later, when the English philosopher Francis Bacon showed that his photic sneeze had nothing to do with heat. If he closed his eyes when going into the sun, he didn’t sneeze even though the heat was still there.

Henry Everett, a consultant psychiatrist at Johns Hopkins University Hospital in Baltimore, was the first to make a systematic attempt to understand the condition, noting in 1964 that 30% of the staff employed in the medical department were photic sneezers. Everett did some further investigation. He found that while 80% of sneezes reported other sneezes among their relatives, only 20% of non-sneezers did.

Now there are factors that are certain indicators of a photic sneeze, first of all, those with the condition almost always sneeze a set number of times on exposure to light. In addition to this, the sneeze depends on a contrast in visible brightness, such as when the sun moves out from behind a cloud. And the sneezing fit won’t be repeated immediately. The body needs time before it can be recharged, so if you go back into a darkened space and then immediately re-enter bright light, you will not sneeze again.

Now onto possible applications of research in this area. The photic sneeze had long been overlooked because its effects are generally less than serious, although the government did once study it as a risk factor for pilots. Yet work on such a simple disorder might lead to important discoveries on more acute conditions such as migraine or epilepsy, which are also caused by cross wires in the nervous system. That is why I encourage you to select something similar for your first investigative medical project. It could be the beginning of something even more useful.

analyses.content: 原文提到这种反应的一个症状是呼吸频率增加（increase in their breathing rate），频率增加对应的就是题目中的“更快（faster）”。
The reaction of some people is immediate, an unpleasant prickling in the nose, an increase in their breathing rate, and an uncontrollable watering of the eyes.
你可能听到了 "rate"，但题目结构是 "faster ... "，这里填 "breathing"（呼吸）才能构成完整的“呼吸变快”的语义，只填 rate 语意不明。
This so-called photic or light sneeze is a reflex, which means it can't be controlled, and it's very common, anything between one in ten and one in three people might be affected.
题目问的是这是一种什么样的反射（形容词），不要被后面的数字（one in ten）干扰，直接抓形容词 "common"。
录音中紧接着说这种反射“非常普遍”（it's very common），并给出了每三到十人中就有一人受影响的数据来支持。
The result is a cascade of reactions, beginning with the stimulation of the nerve endings all over the face, and generating an explosive expulsion of air at up to 95 miles an hour...
虽然前面提到了 "nostrils"（鼻孔），但题目特定问的是 "Nerve endings in the..."（哪里的神经末梢），录音明确对应的是 Face。
录音详细描述了喷嚏的连锁反应，始于遍布脸部（all over the face）的神经末梢受到刺激。
The body's coordination of such reactions is complicated and belongs to the subconscious control hardware that regulates other things, for example tears in the eyes.
不要填 "eyes"，题目问的是 "production of..."（产生什么），显然是产生眼泪，而不是产生眼睛。
录音提到这种身体协调机制属于潜意识控制硬件，它也调节其他事物，例如眼泪（tears）的产生。
The Greek philosopher Aristotle asked, why does the sun prompt us to sneeze, whereas the heat of a fire does not?
题目是拿 "sun" 和另一个具体事物做对比，不要填 "heat"，因为 heat 是这两个事物的共同属性（或者说差异点），对比的主体是 fire。
亚里士多德提出疑问：为什么太阳会引发喷嚏，而火的热量（heat of a fire）却不会？
Everett 发现 80% 的光喷嚏者报告说他们的亲戚（among their relatives）也有这个习惯。
He found that while 80% of sneezers reported other sneezes among their relatives, only 20% of non-sneezers did.
不要主观臆断填 "family" 或 "parents"，雅思填空要求“所听即所得”，录音原词是 relatives。
Now there are factors that are certain indicators of a photic sneeze, first of all, those with the condition almost always sneeze a set number of times on exposure to light.
不要只听到 "times"，题目结构是 "the same ... of sneezes"，这里需要填核心名词 number。
录音说患有此症的人在接触光线时，几乎总是打固定次数（set number of times）的喷嚏。
In addition to this, the sneeze depends on a contrast in visible brightness, such as when the sun moves out from behind a cloud.
题目问的是 "caused by a ... in brightness"，即亮度的某种变化状态，答案是 contrast 而不是 light 或 sun。
录音明确指出，打喷嚏取决于可见亮度的对比（contrast in visible brightness），比如太阳从云后出来。

And the sneezing fit won’t be repeated immediately. The body needs time before it can be recharged, so if you go back into a darkened space and then immediately re-enter bright light, you will not sneeze again.
题目中 "take" 对应录音中的 "need"，这是一个非常经典的时间表达同义替换。
录音说身体需要时间（needs time）才能重新充电，所以喷嚏不会立刻重复。
The photic sneeze had long been overlooked because its effects are generally less than serious, although the government did once study it as a risk factor for pilots.
注意听前面的 "government did once study it"，不要误填为 government，题目问的是 "among..."（在哪些人群中），即研究对象是 pilots。
录音提到政府曾经研究过它，将其作为飞行员（pilots）的一个风险因素。
